title: Bless, O Lord, Each Opening Year
description: Bless, O Lord, Each Opening Year in Tonic Solfa to HEINLEIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 566, “New Year”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HEINLEIN; any other Sevens (7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Bless, O Lord, each open-ing year To the souls as-sem-bling here: Clothe Thy word with power di-vine, Make us will-ing to be Thine.

lines: Bless, O Lord, each opening year
Clothe Thy word with power divine,
Make us willing to be Thine.
Where Thou hast Thy work begun,
Give new strength the race to run;
Bless us all, both old and young;
Call forth praise from every tongue:
All Thy power and all Thy love!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to HEINLEIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
